Apple___Apple_scab: Remove and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to reduce fungal spores. Apply a fungicide such as captan or myclobutanil starting at bud break, repeating every 7-10 days during wet spring weather.
Apple___Black_rot: Prune out dead or cankered wood. Remove mummified/rotted fruit from branches and the ground. Apply fungicide sprays during the growing season, especially after rainfall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust: Remove nearby host plants that carry the fungus if possible. Apply a protective fungicide from early bud stage through early summer.
Apple___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain regular watering, balanced fertilization, and periodic pruning to support continued healthy growth.
Blueberry___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain acidic, well-drained soil and consistent watering.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew: Improve air circulation by pruning dense growth. Apply a sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate fungicide at the first sign of white powdery patches.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy: No treatment needed. Continue regular pruning and consistent watering.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray: Rotate with non-host crops each season. Choose resistant varieties where possible. Apply a foliar fungicide if symptoms appear early under humid conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_: Choose resistant varieties. Fungicide is usually only needed if rust appears early on young growth during cool, wet conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight: Rotate crops and clear plant debris after harvest to reduce fungal spores. Use resistant varieties and apply fungicide promptly if symptoms appear.
Corn_(maize)___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain proper spacing and crop rotation.
Grape___Black_rot: Remove infected fruit and leaves. Apply fungicide starting at early growth through mid-season, especially during wet periods.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles): No cure exists once established — remove and destroy severely affected sections. Avoid pruning during wet weather to reduce new infections.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo: Improve airflow through pruning. Apply a copper-based or other labeled fungicide at the first sign of symptoms.
Grape___healthy: No treatment needed. Continue routine care and monitoring.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening): No cure exists. Remove and destroy severely affected plants to prevent spread. Control the insect that spreads this disease using approved insecticides, and use only certified disease-free planting stock going forward.
Peach___Bacterial_spot: Choose resistant varieties where available. Apply a copper-based treatment during dormant and early growing periods; avoid overhead watering.
Peach___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain regular pruning and balanced fertilization.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot: Use disease-free seed or transplants. Avoid overhead watering. Apply a copper-based treatment at first symptoms, and rotate growing areas yearly.
Pepper,_bell___healthy: No treatment needed. Continue consistent watering and monitoring.
Potato___Early_blight: Rotate growing areas yearly. Remove infected leaves. Apply a fungicide such as chlorothalonil at first symptoms.
Potato___Late_blight: This spreads quickly — remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Apply preventive fungicide during cool, wet weather. Avoid overhead watering.
Potato___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain proper soil mounding and consistent watering.
Raspberry___healthy: No treatment needed. Continue regular pruning for airflow.
Soybean___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain crop rotation practices.
Squash___Powdery_mildew: Improve air circulation between plants. Apply sulfur, neem oil, or potassium bicarbonate spray at the first sign of white powdery patches.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest. Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead watering. Apply fungicide if symptoms are severe.
Strawberry___healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain mulching and consistent watering.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot: Use disease-free seed. Avoid working with wet foliage. Apply a copper-based treatment early, and rotate growing areas yearly.
Tomato___Early_blight: Remove lower infected leaves. Apply mulch to prevent soil splash onto leaves. Apply fungicide such as chlorothalonil or a copper-based product at first symptoms.
Tomato___Late_blight: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent spread. Apply preventive fungicide during cool, wet conditions. Avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold: Improve ventilation to reduce humidity. Remove infected leaves. Apply fungicide if humid conditions persist.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot: Remove infected lower leaves promptly. Apply mulch around the base. Apply fungicide such as chlorothalonil at first sign of small spots with dark borders.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider: Spray affected areas with water to dislodge mites. Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil. Introduce natural predatory insects if infestation is heavy.
Tomato___Target_Spot: Remove infected leaves and improve air circulation. Apply fungicide at first symptoms; avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus: No cure exists — remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread. Wash hands and tools after handling infected material, and control sap-feeding insects that can spread it.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus: No cure exists — remove and destroy infected plants. Control the insect that spreads this virus using insecticidal soap, sticky traps, or approved insecticides.
Tomato___healthy: No treatment needed. Continue regular watering, support staking, and monitoring for early signs of pests or disease.
